The belt was not broken but had lost tension, causing the fan to stall intermittently. The fan motor was running but the belt was slipping on the pulley. The high condenser pressure was caused by reduced airflow over the condenser coil due to the fan not rotating at full speed.

The belt is the same one that was re-tensioned on 06/07/2026 after initial running. At that time, the belt was in acceptable condition. The condenser coil was inspected visually. No fouling was observed. The coil was chemically washed on 08/07/2026, and the approach temperature has been stable since 09/07/2026. documents.content:
At 14:40, Chiller Unit CH-01 tripped. The trip was recorded in the BMS as a high condenser pressure fault. The chiller was running at approximately 88% load at the time of the trip, per the last logged reading at 14:30. The condenser approach temperature was 4.3°C at 14:30, which is within the normal range of 4.2–4.5°C. No abnormal vibration or noise was reported before the trip.

On inspection, the cooling tower fan on CT-02 was found stopped. The fan belt was found worn, with visible cracking on the inner surface. The belt was not broken but had lost tension, causing the fan to stall intermittently. The fan motor was running but the belt was slipping on the pulley. The high condenser pressure was caused by reduced airflow over the condenser coil due to the fan not rotating at full speed.

The belt is the same one that was re-tensioned on 06/07/2026 after initial running. At that time, the belt was in acceptable condition. The worn condition observed today is consistent with accelerated wear following the earlier trip on 05/07/2026, when the same belt was noted as a contributing factor to high condenser pressure. The belt was not replaced at that time because the wear was not considered severe enough. This assessment was incorrect in hindsight.

The fan belt was removed for inspection. The belt will be replaced with a new one from stores. The replacement is scheduled for 16/07/2026. The new belt has been requested from stores and confirmation of receipt is pending. The part number is the same as the one used previously: MB-4500. The pulley was inspected and shows minor wear on the motor-side pulley, as noted on 08/07/2026. No further deterioration was observed. The pulley wear is not considered a contributing factor to the belt failure.

The condenser coil was inspected visually. No fouling was observed. The coil was chemically washed on 08/07/2026, and the approach temperature has been stable since 09/07/2026. The condenser pressure was within normal range at 14:30, confirming that the coil condition was not a contributing factor to the trip.

Chiller Unit CH-01 tripped_at 2026-07-15T14:40:00+05:30. Record status: historical.

The chiller was not restarted after the trip. The chiller will remain offline until the belt is replaced and the cooling tower fan is confirmed to be operating at full speed. The compressor is not suspected to be damaged. No unusual readings were observed on the compressor during the trip event. The oil pressure and temperature were normal at the time of the trip. The oil sample that was sent for lab analysis on 11/07/2026 is still pending results. This sample was taken as part of routine monitoring and is not related to the trip.

The BMS power blip at 14:35 is not believed to be related to the chiller trip. The blip affected only communication to AHU-02, AHU-03, and pump P-04. All three units restarted automatically and have been operating normally since. The chiller did not lose power during the blip. The chiller trip occurred at 14:40, five minutes after the blip, and was caused by the high condenser pressure fault. The blip is considered a coincidence.

The false alarm from FAP-03 at 14:23 is also not related to the chiller trip. The false alarm was investigated and no fire condition was found. The panel was reset. The suspected cause is a faulty smoke sensor in the basement corridor. The sensor will be replaced on 16/07/2026. The false alarm did not affect the chiller or the cooling tower.

Action items:

1. Replace fan belt on CT-02 on 16/07/2026. Confirmation of receipt from stores pending.
2. Inspect and re-tension the new belt after 24 hours of operation.
3. Monitor condenser approach temperature after restart. Target range 4.2–4.5°C.
4. Replace smoke sensor on FAP-03 on 16/07/2026.
5. Continue monitoring AHU-02, AHU-03, and pump P-04 for any issues following the power blip.
6. Review the belt inspection procedure to avoid similar missed wear in the future.
